purpose: Test whether prioritizing within-family near-optimal versus non-near-optimal pairs improves held-family top-10 quality ranking
hypothesis_not_established_cause: Continuous regret pairs may dilute scarce near-optimal distinctions
label_rule: 100 * total_cycles <= 101 * fitting_family_min_cycles; positive integer cycles only
evaluation: Six leave-one-family-out folds; primary descriptive result excludes exhaustive s35932; seeds are not independent families
changed_component: CandidateMLP quality pair construction; real worker/runner implemented and independently reviewed with low-memory guard
pair_order: SHA-256 canonical family and positive/negative UID pair, deterministic tie-break
cap_rationale: Fixed engineering bound, not tuned on results
family_loss: Equal fitting-family macro weight; equal pair weight within each fitting family
score_direction: Higher score ranks earlier; softplus(score_negative - score_positive) decreases when a positive is scored above a negative
features: Unchanged sealed seven-feature allowlist; outcome fields never candidate features
controls: Archived v3 CandidateMLP, fixed heuristic and XGBoost; do not refit controls or choose seeds
decision_rule: Report every held-family result and baseline difference; no post-hoc numeric pass threshold or causal/generalization claim
cost_boundary: No runtime input to quality loss or score division; lower cost on no-hit runs is not evidence of speedup
next_release_scope: After local implementation review, propose exactly 18 TRAIN-only CandidateMLP fits with unchanged architecture, epochs, optimizer and normalization, locked new B root and persisted request/freeze binding; require reviewed integrated synthetic path before release
